evidence.observation: The offline build entry point is the package-local script `build:offline`: `npm run check:model-data && tsgo -p tsconfig.build.json && shx rm -rf dist/providers/data && shx cp -r src/providers/data dist/providers/data`. It never invokes `generate-models`, so no upstream HTTP fetch happens; it consumes already-present hydrated JSON, type-strips it into `dist`, and then copies the (non-TypeScript) hydrated data directory into the compiled output because the compiler does not emit JSON assets.

`hydrate-model-data` runs `node scripts/generate-models.ts --strict --data-only`. The `--data-only` flag is the hydration mode: it fetches upstream model values and writes only the ignored JSON value files, leaving the committed generated TypeScript wrappers untouched. This is the network-dependent step that `build:offline` deliberately skips.

`generate-models` runs `node scripts/generate-models.ts --strict`: the full generation mode that rewrites both the committed generated TypeScript (`src/models.generated.ts` and `src/providers/*.models.ts`) and the ignored JSON value data. Contrasting this with `hydrate-model-data` (same script, `--data-only`) is what separates the generated artifact from the hydrated artifact.

`build` is `npm run generate-models && npm run build:offline`. The two halves make the split explicit: `generate-models` is the online half that refreshes hydrated data (and generated catalogs), while the tail `build:offline` is a pure-compile half that reuses whatever data is on disk. `npm run build:offline` is therefore exactly `build` minus the network step.

`check:model-data` runs `node scripts/check-model-data.ts` and is the first command of `build:offline`. It is the offline gate: it validates that the hydrated JSON matches the generated catalog (shard set, per-file hashes, manifest structure hash) and exits non-zero when the data is missing or stale, so an offline build fails fast instead of compiling against absent data.

The publish allowlist is `["dist", "README.md"]`. Neither `src/` nor the generated TypeScript is published, so the hydrated JSON must be materialised inside `dist/providers/data` by `build:offline` for the packed artifact to carry model values. This is why the offline build ends with an explicit `cp -r src/providers/data dist/providers/data`.

The whole `scripts` block enumerates every producer and consumer of the artifact classes: `clean` (`shx rm -rf dist`) discards build output, `generate-models`/`hydrate-model-data`/`generate-model-catalog` produce artifacts, `check:model-data` validates, `build` is online, `build:offline` is offline, and `prepublishOnly` (`clean && build`) guarantees a fresh online build before packing.

`generate-model-catalog` uses `--json-only --json-output ../../.artifacts/model-catalog`, emitting a third, throwaway JSON catalog into the ignored `.artifacts/` tree used for publishing/comparing the catalog. It confirms the generator has three mutually exclusive output modes (full, data-only, json-only), of which only the data-only/hydrated output is required by the offline build.

Parses `--strict`, `--data-only`, `--json-only`, `--pretty`, `--json-output` and rejects unknown arguments; it also forbids combining `--data-only` with JSON catalog output. This is the single switch that decides whether the run writes generated TypeScript, hydrated JSON, or both.

In `--data-only` (hydration) mode the provider id set is derived from the already-committed generated aggregator via `readModelDataProviderIds(packageRoot)` rather than from upstream discovery. Hydration is therefore anchored to the generated artifact: `Cannot hydrate missing providers: ...` is thrown if the fetched upstream data does not cover a provider the generated catalog declares.

Hydrated values are written to a temporary staging directory (`mkdtempSync(join(providersDir, ".model-generation-"))`), a `.manifest.json` is created from the structure plus per-file SHA-256 hashes, and the staged directory is validated before it is atomically swapped into `src/providers/data`. The `.model-generation-*` staging path is itself git-ignored.

Before overwriting committed generated TypeScript, the previous shard contents and aggregator are captured so the run can roll back on failure. This transactional behaviour exists because the `.models.ts` shards and `src/models.generated.ts` are real source-controlled files (unlike the ignored hydrated JSON), so a half-written generated tree would show up as a dirty git diff.

Each generated shard is emitted with the literal header `// This file is auto-generated by scripts/generate-models.ts` / `// Do not edit manually - run 'npm run generate-models' to update`, then `import values from "./data/<provider>.json" with { type: "json" }` and three `flatten*ModelCatalog` exports. The shard is a committed wrapper whose only job is to derive exact literal types from the ignored JSON keys; the values themselves live in the hydrated file.

Defines `MODEL_DATA_SCHEMA_VERSION = 6` and `MODEL_DATA_MANIFEST_FILE = ".manifest.json"` plus the `ModelDataManifest` shape (`schemaVersion`, `generatedAt`, `structureHash`, `files` hash map). The manifest is the stamp that lets an offline build prove its hydrated data matches the generated catalog without contacting the network.

Reads `src/models.generated.ts` and regex-extracts the classifier/image/chat import lines to recover the provider id list. This is the coupling that makes the generated TypeScript authoritative over the hydrated data: hydration and validation both enumerate providers from the committed generated aggregator.

Entry point used both by the offline gate and by the generator itself after a swap: `readModelDataStructure` + `validateModelDataDirectory` over `src/providers/data`. It checks file set equality with the generated catalog, manifest schema version, the structure hash, per-file SHA-256 hashes, API grouping, and per-model field validity.

The offline gate script. It wraps `validateGeneratedModelData(packageRoot)` in a try/catch that prints the underlying error and the remediation hint `Model data is missing or stale. Run npm run hydrate:model-data from the repository root.` and sets a non-zero exit code. This is what makes `build:offline` fail deterministically when hydrated data is absent.

`MODELS` is the aggregate re-export map built from the generated provider shards (`readonly "<provider>": typeof <PROVIDER>_MODELS`), with sibling `IMAGE_MODELS` and `CLASSIFIER_MODELS` maps later in the file. The file opens (lines 1-2) with the auto-generation banner `This file is auto-generated by scripts/generate-models.ts` / `Do not edit manually`, so it is generated-but-tracked: machine-produced yet committed to the source tree, unlike the ignored hydrated JSON.

A representative generated shard: auto-generation header, a JSON import from `./data/openai.json` (a file that does not exist in a fresh source checkout because it is git-ignored), and `export const OPENAI_MODELS: ChatModelCatalog<typeof values, "openai"> = flattenChatModelCatalog("openai", values)`. This single file embodies the generated/hydrated split.

Maps the raw JSON group shape to a typed catalog keyed by model id, resolving the owning API from the group the key sits in. It is hand-written source that gives the hydrated JSON its static type, which is why the generated shards can stay tiny and churn-free while the values live in ignored data.

Two ignored paths define the artifact boundaries: `packages/*/dist/` (line 8, build output) and `packages/ai/src/providers/data/` (line 11, hydrated JSON values). The generated TypeScript wrappers are pointedly not listed, which is what makes them tracked source-controlled artifacts rather than ignored output.

Development docs state the contract verbatim: `npm run build` refreshes model data, then builds all packages; `npm run build:offline` rebuilds using existing model data without network access. This is the user-facing statement that the offline path consumes, and does not produce, hydrated data.

Records the design decision: model catalogs keep TypeScript model shapes separate from ignored JSON model values to reduce generated source churn, and `npm run build` refreshes model data while `npm run build:offline` reuses existing data without network access. It documents the intended three-way split between source, generated shapes, and hydrated values.

The build config compiles `src/**/*.ts` into `./dist` with `rootDir: ./src`. Since TypeScript/tsgo emits only JavaScript and declarations, the JSON hydrated data has no representation in `dist` unless it is copied, which is exactly why `build:offline` performs the extra `shx cp -r src/providers/data dist/providers/data`.

The source-archive tooling requires `packages/ai/src/providers/data/.manifest.json` plus at least one provider JSON, aborts with `Generated model data is missing. Run npm run hydrate:model-data first.`, and then force-adds those ignored files into a temporary index (`git add -f --`) so `git archive` ships the hydrated artifact inside an otherwise source-only tarball.

When `--offline-model-data` sets `OFFLINE_MODEL_DATA=true` the script runs `npm run build:offline` instead of `npm run build`, printing `Building all packages with bundled model data...`. This is the consumer of the archive-produced hydrated data: extract archive, build offline, no network.

The monorepo root mirrors the split across all workspaces: `build` chains each package's normal build (and `packages/ai`'s online `build`), while `build:offline` chains `packages/ai`'s `build:offline`, and separate `generate:models` / `hydrate:model-data` / `check:model-data` / `generate:model-catalog` aliases delegate into the ai package. Hydration is a distinct, explicitly-invoked prerequisite for every offline build.

claims.claim: In packages/ai the hydrated artifact is the JSON model-value directory `src/providers/data/`, produced only by the `hydrate-model-data` script (`generate-models.ts --strict --data-only`); it is git-ignored and therefore is not source, even though `generate-models` metadata lives in the committed package manifest.

`build:offline` is genuinely offline: it validates existing hydrated data (`check:model-data`), compiles with tsgo, and copies `src/providers/data` into `dist/providers/data`, and it never calls `generate-models`, so issuing it on a machine without network still succeeds provided the hydrated data is present.

The generated artifact class is the committed TypeScript produced by `generate-models`: `src/models.generated.ts` plus 42 `src/providers/*.models.ts` shards, each carrying the `auto-generated ... Do not edit manually` banner and importing the ignored `./data/<provider>.json`; they are tracked in git (unlike the hydrated JSON) and are regenerated transactionally with rollback.

The split is mirrored monorepo-wide: the root `package.json` chains each workspace's ordinary build under `build` but routes `packages/ai` through `build:offline` under `build:offline`, and exposes `hydrate:model-data` / `check:model-data` / `generate:models` as separate aliases, so hydration remains an explicit, out-of-band prerequisite rather than part of any offline path.

`check:model-data` is the offline precondition gate: it re-derives the provider list from the committed generated aggregator and verifies the hydrated directory's file set, manifest schema version, structure hash and per-file SHA-256 hashes, instructing the user to run `npm run hydrate:model-data` when the data is missing or stale.

Build output (`dist/`) is a third artifact class distinct from the hydrated JSON: tsgo emits only JS/d.ts under `outDir: ./dist`, so `build:offline` explicitly removes and re-copies `src/providers/data` into `dist/providers/data`, and `.gitignore` excludes both `packages/*/dist/` and the hydrated source directory.

Because the hydrated data is ignored but required for a network-free build, release tooling force-adds it into the source archive (`git add -f` on `src/providers/data/.manifest.json` and `*.json`) and the binary build script then selects `npm run build:offline` under `--offline-model-data`, reconstructing a complete offline build from an otherwise source-only checkout.

The published package cannot rely on the source tree: the `files` allowlist is only `["dist", "README.md"]`, so hydrated values must be embedded into `dist` by the offline build step for consumers to get model data.

The offline contract is documented identically in user-facing docs and in the changelog: `npm run build` refreshes model data (network), while `npm run build:offline` reuses existing data without network access, with TypeScript model shapes kept separate from ignored JSON model values to reduce generated source churn.

conclusion: In the `pi` monorepo's `packages/ai`, the artifacts split three ways. (1) Source: hand-written TypeScript under `src/` (providers/*.ts, models.ts, types.ts, model-catalog.ts) and the generator scripts under `scripts/`, all tracked in git. (2) Generated: the TypeScript catalogs written by `scripts/generate-models.ts` — `src/models.generated.ts` and the 42 `src/providers/<id>.models.ts` shards — which carry an explicit `auto-generated / Do not edit manually` banner and are committed to git even though they are machine-produced; generation is transactional with rollback because these files appear in diffs. (3) Hydrated: the JSON model values in `src/providers/data/<id>.json` plus `.manifest.json`, written by `generate-models.ts --strict --data-only` (the `hydrate-model-data` script) from live upstream sources such as models.dev, and deliberately git-ignored. The distinction matters for an offline build because `packages/ai`'s `build:offline` script performs only `check:model-data` (validate the hydrated data against the generated catalog's manifest hashes), `tsgo -p tsconfig.build.json`, and `shx cp -r src/providers/data dist/providers/data` — it never invokes `generate-models`, so it makes no network requests and depends on hydrated data already being on disk. `build` is simply `generate-models && build:offline`, i.e. the online refresh prepended to the same offline tail, and the root `build:offline`/`build` scripts mirror that choice across all workspaces. Since tsgo only emits JS/d.ts and the package publishes only `dist` + README, the hydrated JSON has to be copied into `dist/providers/data` explicitly; and because the hydrated directory is git-ignored yet required, release tooling force-adds it (`git add -f`) into the source archive so `--offline-model-data` builds can reproduce the catalog without contacting upstream. In this source checkout the hydrated directory is absent, which is exactly why the offline gate fails until `npm run hydrate:model-data` is run.

validation.notes: Ran the offline gate that is the first step of `npm run build:offline` (`npm run check:model-data` in packages/ai). Exit code 1 with: "amazon-bedrock.json is not valid JSON: ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '.../packages/ai/src/providers/data/amazon-bedrock.json'" followed by "Model data is missing or stale. Run `npm run hydrate:model-data` from the repository root." This is the correct and expected outcome for a source-only checkout: the hydrated artifact is git-ignored, so the offline build cannot proceed until hydration has run — confirming the source/generated/hydrated separation. Supporting checks: `git ls-files packages/ai/src/providers/*.models.ts | wc -l` = 42 tracked generated shards and `git ls-files packages/ai/src/models.generated.ts` returns the generated aggregator, while `git ls-files packages/ai/src/providers/data | wc -l` = 0 and the directory does not exist on disk; `git check-ignore -v` maps `packages/ai/src/providers/data/openai.json` to .gitignore:11 and `packages/ai/dist/index.js` to .gitignore:8. Limitation: full `npm run build:offline` could not be executed because the workspace has no node_modules, so the optional dependencies `tsgo` (@typescript/native-preview) and `shx` are unavailable; only the dependency-free Node validation script was run (Node v24.14.0, which strips TypeScript types natively).
